fact: Ministry of the Interior's Valentin Nahimana said on 6 May 2026 Burundi is technically ready to produce biometric national ID cards but awaits adoption of the law governing their use.

The FY2026/27 procurement plan of Burundi's finance and digital economy ministry lists recruiting a contractor to set up a national digital identity system, BIF 8,902,999,980 on the state budget, by international open tender.
Burundi is setting up a national digital identity system that is to assign a unique identification number, backed by fingerprint and facial biometrics, according to We Are Tech Africa.
The Directorate General for territorial administration says the State is working on a national digital identity system with a unique identification number, using fingerprints and facial recognition.
The Interior Ministry presented the project for a future national biometric and digital identity card with a unique identification number on 6 May 2026, per SOS Medias Burundi.
system: national biometric and digital identity card

fact: We Are Tech Africa reports Burundian authorities said they have nearly completed the infrastructure for the biometric national ID and await a decree to govern its use.
Burundi Eco reports the biometric national ID project is in a pilot phase in about a dozen communes, to be extended nationwide, with a legal framework still to be revised.
Burundi Eco reports interior ministry officials announced in July 2024 the ID for D project, run under the World Bank-funded PAFEN (USD 92 million), to give each person a unique lifelong ID number.
system: ID for D (Identite pour le Developpement)

fact: Minister Niteretse says a digital identity system is being tested in pilot communes, and a government-commissioned study checks it is inclusive, safe and reliable.
system: digital identity system in pilot communes

fact: Minister Niteretse says the current system does not allow unique identification of persons.
President Evariste Ndayishimiye announced in December 2025 that the digital ID system is being tested in Zone Matara, Gitega province, with nationwide rollout to follow if the pilot succeeds.
The Bank of the Republic of Burundi's Deputy Governor says there is no biometric national ID but the process and its preparatory works are underway.
